evidence.observation: Explains JSON-decoded deadline loss of original Go local monotonic information. At the same supplied points compares 1.8/1.8 s at conversion, 1.4 s original versus 7.4 s decoded epoch before attempt 1, and expired original versus 5.4 s wall remaining later. Distinguishes hosts' monotonic domains and explicitly says the worker converts epoch to duration once; later wall adjustment does not prove its existing timer changes.

Rejects fresh Background-rooted attempt lifetime and missing caller cancellation. Proposes one request-receipt context/deadline capped by earlier parent, retaining original local monotonic deadline across acquisition, attempts, retries and caller cleanup waiting; attempts consume remaining time. Requires parent propagation, stops exhausted/cancelled work and retry only for classified retryable failure with budget and prior completion/safe termination.

Distinguishes process-local monotonic readings from epoch/skew/transit. Supplies a declared custom duration/handoff-age policy: remaining duration reduced by enforced maximum handoff age, local worker timer capped by it and parent, reject zero/too-old admission. Says duration alone renews budget by transit and absent enforced age/cancellation propagation permits only a bounded gateway claim; epoch remains diagnostic absent skew policy. No UTC synchronization or monotonic transfer guarantee.

Explicit proposed controls cover forward/backward wall steps before and after serialization, host skew independently from handoff delay, earlier parent expiry during acquisition/before dispatch/during Lookup, and late completion. Acceptance requires caller outcome by earlier deadline, no expired dispatch/retry, actual Lookup termination or verified disposal, exactly one release, bounded unresolved ownership/escalation and subsequent useful quote. Proposed 100 ms grace limits escalation, not termination/recovery.
